description: 60 heap overflow CVE samples with ground truth labels

cve_01_simple_overflow.notes: Classic fixed-size overflow. write(72+8=80) > alloc(64). Allocator model: usable=80 for 64B request? No, ptmalloc2 usable(64) ≈ 64. Overflow is real.

cve_02_off_by_one.notes: Off-by-one: 33 byte write into 32 byte buffer. Chunk metadata corruption feasible.

cve_03_int_overflow_calc.notes: Integer overflow in size calculation leads to undersized allocation.

cve_04_strcpy_overflow.notes: Unbounded strcpy into fixed-size heap buffer.

cve_05_loop_overflow.notes: Loop counter exceeds allocation size. Cross-function detection needed.

cve_06_user_controlled_size.notes: User controls both allocation and write size. Attacker can make write > alloc.

cve_07_realloc_overflow.notes: Realloc shrinks buffer but code still uses old size assumption.

cve_08_calloc_overflow.pattern: calloc(nmemb, size) with overflow in nmemb*size
cve_08_calloc_overflow.notes: calloc(nmemb, size) integer overflow in internal multiplication.

cve_09_safe_but_triggers_fp.notes: malloc(20) usable=24B (ptmalloc2, prev_size reuse). write offset 24 + 8B = 32 > 24 → overflow. Original FP test assumed usable=32 but glibc prev_size reuse gives 24.

cve_10_input_constrained_safe.notes: Guard condition bounds the size. Constraint tracker should filter.

cve_11_memcpy_arith_size.pattern: malloc(K) + memcpy(dst, src, n*sizeof(X)) where n*sizeof > K
cve_11_memcpy_arith_size.notes: Arithmetic expression in memcpy size. Expression evaluator needed.

cve_12_alignment_edge.pattern: malloc(16) write offset 14 (4 bytes) → within usable
cve_12_alignment_edge.notes: malloc(16) usable=24 (ptmalloc2, prev_size reuse). write offset 14 + 4B = 18 <= 24 → safe. Tests alignment boundary awareness.

cve_13_struct_field_pattern.pattern: struct with field offset > alloc size
cve_13_struct_field_pattern.notes: sizeof(MyStruct)=80, tail at offset 72 + 8B = 80 <= 80 → safe. Tests struct sizeof detection.

cve_14_multi_chunk.pattern: Multiple adjacent malloc + overflow crosses chunk boundary
cve_14_multi_chunk.notes: Multi-chunk scenario. Overflow in chunk A corrupts chunk B metadata.

cve_15_constrained_input.pattern: malloc(n) with if(n<16) guard BUT write > 16
cve_15_constrained_input.notes: Guard exists but insufficient. n<16 → malloc can be 1-15, write is 32B. Real overflow.

cve_16_real_world_pattern.pattern: Complex real-world: nested alloc + indirect write
cve_16_real_world_pattern.notes: Real-world code pattern. Multi-function, indirect pointer manipulation.

cve_17_multi_field_struct.pattern: Struct with multiple pointer fields, field confusion
cve_17_multi_field_struct.notes: sizeof(LargeStruct)=96, checksum at offset 88 + 8B = 96 <= 96 → safe. Tests multi-field struct access.

cve_18_loop_accumulate.notes: Loop accumulation: each individual write safe but total exceeds alloc.

cve_19_same_offset_accumulate.notes: Same-offset write: all writes to buf[0..63] within 256B. consumed grows but destination unchanged. SAFE.

cve_20_cross_func_guard.pattern: alloc in funcA with guard n<=128, write in funcB
cve_20_cross_func_guard.notes: Cross-function guard constraint: n<=128, write=n<=128 < usable(128). Tests interproc CJ.

cve_21_cross_func_write.pattern: malloc(32) in main, memcpy 128B in callee
cve_21_cross_func_write.notes: Cross-function write: alloc 32B, callee copies 128B. Tests interproc constraint propagation.

cve_22_fm_boundary_safe.notes: FM boundary derivation: m<=56, write_end=m+4<=60 < usable(64)=72. Tests FM boundary refine.

cve_23_fm_boundary_overflow.notes: FM boundary derivation: m>=40, write_end=m+4>=44 > usable(32)=40. Tests FM boundary overflow detection.

cve_24_multiple_constraints.pattern: malloc(n) n<=256, off<=200, sz<=56, memcpy(buf+off, src, sz)
cve_24_multiple_constraints.notes: Multiple constraints joined: write_end=off+sz<=256 < usable(256)=264. Tests multi-constraint CJ.

cve_25_nested_loop_overflow.notes: Nested loop: 16*10=160 > usable(128)=136. Tests nested loop bound analysis.

cve_26_realloc_grow_safe.pattern: malloc(32) realloc(256) memcpy at offset 200 size 56
cve_26_realloc_grow_safe.notes: Realloc grows buffer: write_end=200+56=256 < usable(256)=264. Tests realloc size tracking.

cve_27_struct_array_overflow.notes: Struct array OOB: arr[8] at offset 128 > usable(64)=72. Tests sizeof*count multiplication.

cve_28_guarded_loop_safe.notes: Guarded loop: n<=200, write_end=n<=200 < usable(256)=264. Tests loop+guard interaction.

cve_29_alignment_slack_safe.notes: Alignment slack: write_end=52 <= usable(48)=56. Tests glibc request2size precision.

cve_30_cross_func_alloc_only.pattern: make_buf(64) in funcA, write offset 72 in main
cve_30_cross_func_alloc_only.notes: Cross-function alloc: factory function malloc(64), caller writes at 72. Tests interproc alloc tracking.

cve_31_copy_size_external.pattern: malloc(64) memcpy(buf, src, len) len from argv
cve_31_copy_size_external.notes: External copy size: len unconstrained. Conservatively INCONCLUSIVE (kept as candidate). Ground truth: vulnerable because attacker controls len.

cve_32_deeply_nested_safe.notes: Deeply nested: n<=100 off<=40, write_end=off+56<=96 < usable(128)=136. Tests deep interproc.

cve_33_cross_path_guard_safe.pattern: if(n>64)memcpy(64) else return; guard in else path
cve_33_cross_path_guard_safe.notes: Guard in else branch, write in if branch. memcpy 64 <= usable(64)=72. PS-CJ: write path has no guard, 64<=72 → SAFE.

cve_34_cross_path_guard_overflow.notes: Guard in else branch. Write path: memcpy 80 > usable(64)=72 → OVERFLOW. PS-CJ should catch this.

cve_35_early_return_safe.notes: Early return on guard path. Write path: n<=100, memcpy 96 <= usable(128)=136 → SAFE.

cve_36_early_return_overflow.notes: Early return but write path still overflows: memcpy 64 > usable(32)=40 → OVERFLOW.

cve_37_nested_branch_safe.notes: Two write paths: path1 memcpy 128 <= usable(256)=264; path2 memcpy 64 <= 264. Both SAFE.

cve_38_nested_branch_overflow.notes: Two write paths: path1 memcpy 80 > usable(64)=72 → OVERFLOW; path2 memcpy 32 <= 72 → SAFE. PS-CJ catches overflow path.

cve_39_loop_guard_cross_path.notes: Guard in alloc function, loop write in write function. n=80, loop_write=80 <= usable(80)=88 → SAFE.

cve_40_multi_guard_safe.pattern: guard size<=200 + guard offset<=64; memcpy(offset, size); malloc(256)
cve_40_multi_guard_safe.notes: Two independent guards. worst case offset=64+size=200=264 <= usable(256)=264 → SAFE (exactly at boundary).

cve_56_sfod_field_safe.pattern: sizeof(Msg) alloc, buf->b at offset 16 size 16
cve_56_sfod_field_safe.notes: SFOD: struct field offset domain, buf->b offset=16+16=32 <= usable(36)=40 → SAFE. Tests SFOD field offset injection into CJ.

cve_57_sfod_field_overflow.pattern: malloc(16) LargeHeader*, buf->b at offset 32 size 32
cve_57_sfod_field_overflow.notes: SFOD: buf->b offset=32+32=64 > usable(16)=24 → OVERFLOW. Tests SFOD detecting struct field overflow.

cve_58_sfod_cast_safe.notes: SFOD: cast type inference, buf->data offset=8+24=32 <= usable(32)=40 → SAFE. Tests SFOD cast-based type inference.

cve_59_sfod_cast_overflow.notes: SFOD: buf->body offset=4+32=36 > usable(16)=24 → OVERFLOW. Tests SFOD cast+memcpy overflow.

cve_60_sfod_nested_safe.pattern: sizeof(Wide) alloc, buf->magic at offset 128 size 8
cve_60_sfod_nested_safe.notes: SFOD: nested struct last field, buf->magic offset=128+8=136 <= usable(136)=144 → SAFE. Tests SFOD multi-field offset.

key_fp_challenges: cve_22: FM boundary derivation (guard m<=56, write_end<=60)
cve_24: multiple constraints joined (n<=256, off<=200, sz<=56)
cve_32: deeply nested interproc (3-layer call chain)
cve_33: cross-path guard (guard in else, write in if)
cve_35: early return safe (guard path returns, write path safe)
cve_37: nested branch dual paths (both safe)
cve_39: loop guard cross-path (guard in funcA, loop in funcB)
